featured.title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
featured.tldr: Infrathon gives coding agents 12 to 24 hours on 25 real AI-infrastructure optimization tasks; 135 of 150 runs keep improving in the second half, and one agent tripled a human-designed KV-cache codec's compression.

featured.title: RoboColosseum: Evaluating Physical Intelligence at Scale In-The-Wild
featured.tldr: RoboColosseum runs blinded pairwise robot trials across 124 sites and finds frontier chat agents rival specialized robot policies, while rankings vary across tasks, robots and evaluation tracks.

featured.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
featured.tldr: FrontierPhysics has 42 physicists turn their own research into 56 end-to-end tasks, and no AI agent configuration passes more than 46 of 168 attempts.

featured.title: Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly
featured.tldr: When long-running coding agents summarize their context to keep going, benchmark scores barely change, but the rules they were given quietly disappear from the summaries.

featured.title: VerifierBench: Benchmarking the Generation of Executable Verifiers for LLM Agents
featured.tldr: Across 19 models, agent-written verifiers accept valid solutions less reliably than they reject invalid ones, often because they impose unjustified checks that their own self-tests never challenge.
